doc.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Writing 'The Old New Waltz' and 'Wisdom of the Heart'
summary: Moore tells how his tune was written and received, and recalls 'Wisdom of the Heart' praised by Gil Evans and Alec Wilder.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I’ll try to find it for you. In fact, I think they mentioned your tune here. “The Old New Waltz.” Tell me how that tune came about.

Well I left the country at one point. I actually moved to India in ‘89. I quit playing the bass, and went to India, and ended up in London. It didn’t work out in India, and I ended up in London and was playing piano, but mostly not doing much of anything. And then I started playing bass again over there. But I was spending a lot of time on piano, and I occasionally was coming back to New York. And I spent a lot of time writing around that time, and I didn’t think much of that tune. I knew it worked, it was the kind of thing well I thought well it’s okay. And then we got called to do this recording when I was going to be back. And everybody was supposed to submit a song. And so I mean I didn’t even have it written out properly or anything, so I wrote it out and brought it back. And I have no judgment about the songs that I write. There was a song with Marian McPartland on “Ambiance” called ‘Wisdom of the Heart.” It was I think the first song that I wrote. And it’s just a simple little waltz, very short, kind goes to some interesting place harmonically. And everybody loved that song. I mean people like Gil Evans came up to me and he said, “Have you got any more songs like ‘Wisdom of the Heart?’” And I’m saying wow. Alec Wilder liked the song and wrote me a letter about it. And I’m saying, I don’t get it. But in daylight it was such a thrill, and Marian liked it, and a lot of people liked that song. It was just a short little waltz. And I wrote this one, and I’ve had great response from that. People say oh they love the song. People have written lyrics for it that have really loved that song. Another band, I walked into a place in St. Louis, there was a trio there playing this song. It was the first time in my life —

They said, “We’re going to play your song.” And so that had never happened to me before. And so I mean I like it, and I think it’s pretty, but I don’t have any — and it may be one of the best things I’ve written. I don’t write a lot. I mean I write in spurts. But I knew it worked and it was that kind of thing, but I didn’t have any great feeling about it.
